evidence.note: Opened by inspecting data shards (uint16 ~131M tokens), GPU, and reading train_AGENT_template.py before building; correctly identified shard format and adapted the template's checkpoint-loading conventions.
Discovered uint16 CUDA advanced-indexing incompatibility only at runtime — a data-format detail careful orientation could have caught earlier, though promptly diagnosed and patched.

Deliberately verified the full contract: load_model_for_verification loads the int8 checkpoint (dequant round-trip), model(input_ids) returns correct-shape float logits, model(input_ids,targets) matches cross_entropy exactly, plus a position-dependence probe.

Persistent 'rough 4 bytes/token' bpb approximation caused repeated uncertainty about passing; accurate decoded-byte accounting and inspecting the val-shard header to confirm the bpb denominator came late rather than up front.

Explored int4 packing to fit a larger model under the exact 32,000,000-byte cap — deriving the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope, but reactively after struggling rather than as an up-front constraint; only one load path implemented.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5 (read spec/template, identified shard format, exact decimal 32MB cap, one load path, both forward signatures) and reaches most of level 8: it deliberately mapped and verified the loading/forward contract — int8 dequant round-trip, exact cross_entropy match, position-dependence probe — and eventually probed the shard/tokenizer to confirm the bpb denominator. It falls short of a clean 8/10 because a core environment-metric assumption (bytes-per-token for bpb) was approximated rather than probed for much of the run, causing sustained target uncertainty, and the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope and int4 path emerged reactively rather than up front, with only one load path implemented. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.
